name: linux-privacy

cli_commands.cmd: command -v flatpak >/dev/null && flatpak config --user --get report-os-info >/dev/null && flatpak config --user --set report-os-info false
cli_commands.disables: Flatpak OS name/version/architecture reporting in the Flatpak-Os-Info HTTP header for the per-user installation only. Run only if Flatpak is installed and its report-os-info key is supported. This does not disable usage/crash reporting inside applications, downloads, remote server logs or system-installation reporting.

manual_only_items.name: Flatpak system and additional installations
manual_only_items.ui_path: Terminal, only when Flatpak is installed and `flatpak config --system --get report-os-info` supports the key: after administrator approval, run `sudo flatpak config --system --set report-os-info false`; verify with `flatpak config --system --get report-os-info`. For each named installation in /etc/flatpak/installations.d, use `--installation=NAME` instead of `--system`. Verify the per-user installation separately with `flatpak config --user --get report-os-info`.
manual_only_items.reason: Configuration is per installation. The key is present in Flatpak 1.18.4 but absent in 1.16.1; capability-check the installed build rather than guessing from distro name. Old builds without this key do not implement this particular header control. Upstream also documents a no-report-os-info marker in FLATPAK_CONFIG_DIR; the skill does not create system files automatically.

manual_only_items.name: Flatpak application usage and crash reports
manual_only_items.ui_path: For each installed Flatpak application that collects usage/crash reports, use that application's own Privacy, Diagnostics or Feedback settings; KDE applications may expose the KUserFeedback controls below. Record each app's actual setting separately.
manual_only_items.reason: Flatpak's documented report-os-info switch controls a download HTTP header, not a universal application telemetry/crash-reporting agent. Restricting app network permissions can break normal app features and is not applied as a telemetry opt-out. Do not report all Flatpak apps opted out after changing the header setting.

manual_only_items.name: GNOME automatic problem reporting and software-usage statistics
manual_only_items.ui_path: On GNOME with an ABRT-backed reporting service, open Settings → Privacy & Security → Diagnostics and turn Automatic Problem Reporting OFF. If the panel is absent, inspect the distro's reporting agent instead. When the org.gnome.desktop.privacy schema exposes the corresponding keys, the documented settings are `gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.privacy report-technical-problems false` and `gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.privacy send-software-usage-stats false`; verify each with `gsettings get` in the same user's desktop session.
manual_only_items.reason: GNOME's Diagnostics panel watches org.freedesktop.problems.daemon and hides itself when that ABRT service is absent. These settings cover cooperating GNOME/distro integrations, not every crash reporter or package survey. Check schema/key availability first; do not invent a GNOME telemetry service or run these commands on KDE/headless systems.

manual_only_items.name: KDE Plasma and application KUserFeedback
manual_only_items.ui_path: On KDE Plasma, search System Settings for User Feedback and choose the lowest sharing level. Also open each participating application's User Feedback settings (for example Dolphin → Configure Dolphin → User Feedback), set statistics to Don't share anything and surveys to Don't participate. For an administrator-managed KUserFeedback switch, merge `[UserFeedback]` / `Enabled=false` into /etc/xdg/KDE/UserFeedback.conf, preserving other groups and reviewing any per-user overrides, then restart the participating applications and inspect their feedback settings.
manual_only_items.reason: The official KDE Kiosk documentation describes this global KUserFeedback setting. It applies to clients of that framework, not unrelated KDE apps, distro reporters or all Linux telemetry. Per-application settings and Qt configuration precedence must be checked; the skill does not overwrite an administrator's INI file or remove packages.

manual_only_items.name: Debian-family popularity-contest package survey
manual_only_items.ui_path: Only when popularity-contest is installed: after administrator approval, run `sudo dpkg-reconfigure popularity-contest` and answer No to participation. Verify `PARTICIPATE="no"` in /etc/popularity-contest.conf and inspect /etc/popularity-contest.d/*.conf for overrides.
manual_only_items.reason: The Debian package configuration sets PARTICIPATE from the debconf answer; its scheduled reporter stops when the effective value is no. This is a package-usage survey, separate from GNOME/ABRT and KUserFeedback. Do not install it just to opt out, or generalize this setting to other distributions' agents.

persistent_files.note: Debian-family package-survey participation setting; read only and preserve the host identifier.
Additional survey settings can override participation. Report only; never delete or execute these files.
Administrator-managed KUserFeedback settings. Preserve existing INI groups.
Default per-user Qt/KUserFeedback configuration location; honor XDG_CONFIG_HOME and inspect precedence before claiming the global switch is effective.
Upstream-documented marker when FLATPAK_CONFIG_DIR uses the default system directory; report only.

notes: Inventory the installed desktop, distro and reporting components first. Linux has no universal telemetry opt-out, and no single agent exists on every distribution.

Skip the Flatpak cli_command when its availability/capability checks fail; report not applicable or unsupported rather than claiming an opt-out. Verify the actual per-user value is false after a successful change.

GNOME, KDE and popularity-contest instructions are component-specific manual items. Do not mark absent components opted out, change system settings without approval, uninstall reporting packages or delete existing crash/usage history.
